resolution.note:
Both refuters killed every blocking finding, so the row stamps PASS:verify-refuted and this REVISE stays as the record. research_claims §1 line 8: scope: The judge's facts hold, but check_research_claims.md §1 does not govern this line.

What I confirmed:
- Line 8 of building-agent-systems.md names "(5) Optional: Lindenberg memory-architecture piece" with no URL.
- lectures/module-2-prework.md has zero hits for Lindenberg. It links only Karpathy's gist, at the "Read the memory frame" section.
- The module's maintainer block has no SOURCE NEEDED or NEEDED stamp.
- evals/story-depth/a101-theory-inventory.md logs the piece as "name only, candidate". getting-going.md L66 carries the same wording.

Why §1 does not apply:
1. §1 is about claims. It reads "Every claim gets specific clickable URL + one of [labels]. No URL → mark [SOURCE NEEDED]." Line 8 is an optional reading suggestion in the prework list. It asserts no fact, statistic or practitioner finding, so there is nothing for a label or evidence level to attach to.
2. §1 has an explicit scope clause: "Scope: maintainer-block only, not student-facing body... [label] taxonomy = author/audit vocabulary, not student vocabulary — surfacing in body adds noise." Line 8 is student-facing body. Source stamps belong below `<!-- maintainer -->`, and body prose ships citations in builder voice (§10).
3. The stamp the judge asks for comes from §11 and §11a. §11 is triggered only for a file "carrying practitioner citations — named practitioner + specific URL + load-bearing number". This file has no URL and no number in its body. Karpathy is named in the maintainer block (line 113) with no URL or stamp either, and nobody flagged that. §11a stamps cover "each listed source" in a §11 block, and this file has no such block to hold one. The proposed `[checked:never result:NEEDED due:asap]` therefore has no home under the cited rule.
4. The "debt sits where no tool reads it" harm is overstated. The inventory records it, and learning-rate-vs-model.md L667 and the-leaders-fears.md L565 both list it as a cut candidate ("Optional reading named twice across two files with no consumer"). The maintainer's default is cut, and the usual fix for an unlinked optional reference is a cut or a link, not a §1 block.

The unlocatable pre-read is still a real defect. It belongs under student-facing or pedagogy rules, or a cut pass, and is not a §1 research-claims BLOCK. Filed as BLOCKING under §1 it would push an unwarranted stamp or edit onto a body that is not in violation of the cited rule.
